messages:
priya: Heads up — ran into a weird decrypt failure during a regional failover test. Primary (us-east-1) went unhealthy, app failed over to eu-west-1 replica. We use envelope encryption (DEKs wrapped with an MRK). Most objects decrypt fine but ~2% returned AccessDenied from KMS. Any ideas?
allan: Did you check the DEK cache TTL? If a cached wrapped key references the primary key ARN, trying to call decrypt against the replica could fail.
sara: Worth noting: grants and some key policy conditions are regional. Replica keys don't automatically inherit grants from the primary. If the principal only has a grant on the primary, the replica will reject Decrypt.
priya: Cache TTL is 15m, failover happened ~3m after primary became unhealthy. Logs show AccessDenied from KMS in eu-west-1 and the ciphertext header includes MRK id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh-..
ben-security: Are you using kms:ViaService or kms:EncryptionContext condition keys in the key policy? Cross-account role assumptions + kms:ViaService scoped to a region/service can cause denies when the same principal calls from a different region.
miguel: Also check whether the replica key policy actually lists the redwood service principal or the role. Key policies must explicitly allow the caller in the replica account/region. Grants do not auto-replicate.
allan: Quick repro steps I ran locally: 
```
# encrypt in us-east-1
aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd --plaintext fileb://dek.bin --region us-east-1 --output text --query CiphertextBlob > ct.b64
# simulate failover, try decrypt in eu-west-1
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.b64 --region eu-west-1
```
Observed: AccessDenied from KMS in eu-west-1 until I added an explicit key policy statement for the service role in replica region.
sara: The 2% noise could also come from a rotation/rehydration overlap. If your rewrap job rotated DEKs and some objects were written mid-rotation, some ciphertexts point to keys/grants that didn't exist on the replica yet.
priya: We do run a rewrap job every night; I see an automated run completed ~30s before the failover signal. That could explain mixed headers across objects.
ben-security: Actionable checklist: 
- Confirm replica key policy has the same principal statements as primary (or uses a safe IAM role allowed in both regions/accounts).
- Recreate any necessary grants on the replica (or move to key policy + IAM instead of short-lived grants).
- Harden DEK cache behavior: on AccessDenied do one immediate re-fetch of wrapped DEK (not full fallback every time).
- Add an audit filter for KMS AccessDenied/NotFound for MRK key IDs around failover window.
miguel: FYI when you replicate keys across accounts: you either replicate policies or implement an assume-role flow where the caller assumes a role in the replica account that has decrypt rights in the replica key policy. Grant tokens are also tricky cross-region.
priya: I'm going to open an infra ticket and roll a small client change: when decrypt to replica returns AccessDenied we do a single re-fetch of the wrapped DEK from S3 and attempt decrypt again (with exponential backoff). We'll gate it behind a feature flag.
rotate-bot: rewrap job completed — run id rw-2025-11-03-0300, rewrapped 1.2M objects, duration 18m, rotated key version v20251103
sara: Also add telemetry: log which key ARN is in the ciphertext header and which region endpoint returned the AccessDenied. That helps distinguish policy vs replication lag.
priya: Created INFRA-824 with logs and sample ciphertexts, assigned to @allan and @miguel. I'll follow up with proposed client change and a quick key policy sync. Thanks all :heart:
